sanskrit: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् । तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥
hindiTranslation: हे कुन्तीपुत्र अर्जुन  मनुष्य अन्तकाल में जिसजिस भी भावका स्मरण करते हुए शरीर छोड़ता है वह उस अन्तकालके भावसे सदा भावित होता हुआ उसउसको ही प्राप्त होता है अर्थात् उसउस योनिमें ही चला जाता है ॥
englishTranslation: Whatever state a person remembers at the end, that state is reached, because the mind has been shaped by it.
essence: The end follows the state you have trained.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: The final thought at death shapes where consciousness goes next. A person tends toward whatever state has been cultivated again and again.
simpleInsight: What you repeatedly dwell on becomes the shape of your ending.
detailedMeaning: Krishna deepens the teaching on the final moment: the state of mind at death is the result of a life repeatedly formed by habit and attention.
modernRelevance: A woman who spent forty years worrying about money still asks about the electricity bill from her hospital bed. Krishna's point is that the last thought grows from the thoughts of a lifetime.
translationLiteral: यं यं (whatever) / वा अपि (also indeed) / स्मरन् (remembering) / भावम् (state of being) / त्यजति (abandons) / अन्ते (at the end) / कलेवरम् (the body) / तम् तम् एव (that very) / एति (attains) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / सदा (always) / तद्भावभावितः (formed by that state)
insight: Whatever a person dwells on at the end, Krishna says, they reach, because life has shaped the mind that way.
